findings.summary: Dyagilev nightclub was epicenter of Moscow oligarch socializing; Prokhorov was regular patron
findings.detail: Dyagilev nightclub in Hermitage Garden, Moscow, was created by promoter Alexey Gorobiy and was the most exclusive club of the 2000s. VIP boxes cost 30-40K USD and were occupied by people from Forbes top 10. Regular patrons included Mikhail Prokhorov, Rustam Tariko, Roman Abramovich, government members and deputies. Konchakovskaya was the prima dancer at this club, placing her in direct proximity to Prokhorov and his circle. The club burned down Feb 7, 2008. Art director was Sinisha Lazarevich.

evidence.evidence_ref: Multiple Russian sources confirm Prokhorov was regular Dyagilev patron. Konchakovskaya confirmed as prima dancer. This establishes the social venue connecting them.

findings.summary: Ari in Oct 2018 emails likely refers to Ari Emanuel (WME/Endeavor) — he and Bill Block were both at InterTalent Agency and ICM in early 1990s
findings.detail: The Oct 2018 email (EFTA02619777) references 'mediation reg Bill Block and we had Ari private business discussed.' Bill Block (b.1954) founded InterTalent Agency in 1988. Ari Emanuel joined InterTalent as a partner in 1990. In Oct 1992, Block and 12 associates from InterTalent (including Emanuel) joined ICM, with Block heading West Coast operations. Emanuel was later fired from ICM and founded Endeavor (now WME). Block went on to found Artisan Entertainment, QED International, and became Miramax CEO (2017-2023). Block married Russian model Eugenia Kuzmina (b.1987, Moscow). The sender's reference to Ari private business discussed during mediation with Bill Block strongly suggests Ari Emanuel, given their decades-long professional overlap in Hollywood talent representation.

findings.summary: Analysis: redacted Oct 2018 email sender profile does NOT match Eugenia Kuzmina — Kuzmina still married to Block, no public divorce/custody records
findings.detail: The redacted sender's profile: Russian-speaking woman, has a son, cocaine history, mediation with Bill Block, claims Zampolli fabricated deposition, claims Konchakovskaya lied about virginity/pregnancy, claims 5 heads of states wrote depositions, sent emails at 3:56 AM (European timezone), clearly distressed/erratic, references 'Ari private business.' Eugenia Kuzmina (b.1987 Moscow) is married to Bill Block since March 27 2010 with two children (son Theodore, daughter Veronika). Multiple sources as of Jan 2026 describe the marriage as ongoing — no public divorce filings, custody disputes, or separation found. While Kuzmina matches some criteria (Russian, Moscow, connected to Bill Block, has a son), the absence of any divorce/separation record is a strong counterargument. If they had mediation/custody issues, these would likely be sealed but at minimum some public reference would exist. The sender appears to be a DIFFERENT Russian woman connected to Bill Block/Ari Emanuel's circle — possibly someone from the modeling/entertainment world who had disputes involving Zampolli and depositions.

findings.summary: Bill Block appears on Epstein guest list (Aug 2010) alongside Leon Black, Henry Kravis, Steven Mnuchin — independently confirms Block in Epstein social orbit
findings.detail: EFTA02424126: Guest list titled 'YES LIST - WALL STREET' dated Aug 16, 2010 from Margaux Rogers to jeevacation@gmail.com. Lists 333 people. Entry reads 'Mr. & Mrs. Ed Conard (Jill Davis) / BUSINESS/ LI/ BILL BLOCK/ LITERARY/' — Bill Block appears as a tag/connection notation for the Conard entry. Other notable guests include Leon Black, Henry Kravis, Steven Mnuchin, Wilbur Ross, Kimberly Guilfoyle, Howard Stern, Jeff Zucker, David Koch, Chris Cuomo, Maria Bartiromo, Vicky Ward. This is a high-society event list in Epstein's orbit, confirming Block was known in these circles.

findings.summary: Oleg Baibakov detained with Prokhorov in Courchevel 2007 prostitution raid — confirms long-standing Prokhorov-Baibakov partnership
findings.detail: Jan 9, 2007: French police raided Courchevel ski resort in anti-prostitution operation. 26 people detained including Mikhail Prokhorov (CEO Norilsk Nickel), his assistant Dmitry Shatov, and VP Oleg Baibakov. Seven young Russian women (~20 years old) were also detained. Prokhorov held in Lyon for 4 days, released without charge. Case closed 2 years later for lack of evidence. Baibakov later denied being among the detained through his press secretary, but multiple sources contradict this denial. This confirms the Prokhorov-Baibakov nexus was actively traveling with young Russian women, consistent with the 'Killers' email naming both alongside Zampolli and Konchakovskaya.

evidence.evidence_ref: NBC News Jan 2007, Washington Post Jan 2007, CNBC Jan 2007 reports on Courchevel detention
